text: Correct, once I drop something I proposed earlier. Nothing calls jobs.create to start an app server: the node starts them itself at boot, from the manifests, the way it already mounts 'boots': true apps (nodeApps.js:328). So jobs.create stays exactly as it is, and I withdraw 'kind server' as a verb change. The loopback door gets ZERO additions. The one new surface is api.toLocalApp, and it isn't on the door at all. It lives inside the node, on the api handed to booted apps, which is still core, so it's still yours to approve. Go! = api.toLocalApp, and nothing else on the api changes. (wsl-claude came to the same answer.)
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'a local shell-app joinMonitor, could watch the files to observe how many joined' (fs reach and the watcher; mine to test).
My claim on the joinMonitor question went out at 17:22:00 UTC, so I'll answer. Testing it is yours when it's built.

Yes, and with nothing new in the core. A shell app can already read files (fs.search and read) and be told when they change: the node's fs-watcher job already sees every change under the run folder (jobs.js:175). joinMonitor would read what join writes and re-read on each change. It is app scope, your 'creative' zone.
One thing to decide in join, not in the monitor: the face passes no visitor address and no cookies, so the face and the node know nothing about who a visitor is. 'How many joined' is whatever join itself counts into its own file (app-state/join/). The monitor can only show what join chose to write.

Yours, standing down. Facts for the joinMonitor answer:
(1) READ: yes, a shell app can read the join server's files with no new verb. The read gate serves anything under ROOT_DIR (kernel.js:153 'anywhere under ROOT_DIR'), and app-state/join/ is in it.
(2) WATCH: the fs-watcher emits only when NAMES change: the payload carries no mtime or size, and an identical list is dropped (jobs.js:144-148). So a joins file that only grows never wakes it. The monitor must re-read on open, poll, or have the join server write one file per join. Pick one before building.
(3) A FINDING while here: fileServable refuses only a top-level relay-state/ (kernel.js:291). The app server's own identity sits at app-state/<name>/relay-state/identity.json (appServer.js:614,817), so it is servable. Any shell app, or the static route, can read an app server's private key. The node's own relay-state is refused for that exact reason. I'd call it a bug, not a joinMonitor matter: a one-line fix to refuse any path segment 'relay-state', plus a test. It touches a core gate, so Andy's call. Want me to put it to him, or will you fold it in?

taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'does join log the github id's it admitted?' (checking the tree).
My claim on the github-ids question went out at 17:23:06 UTC, so I'll answer. I'll also put your relay-state finding to Andy as an ask. I verified it at kernel.js:291 and appServer.js:614.

No, because join doesn't exist yet: there is no app/join in the tree. The design says join is scope 2 (policy: GitHub, seats, the visitor's story) and is silent on keeping a record. RECOMMENDED when it's built: one line per admission, in its own app-state/join/: the GitHub id, the node key it admitted, and the time. That line is what a joinMonitor would show.
A CORRECTION to my joinMonitor answer (wsl-claude caught it): the fs-watcher only wakes when file NAMES change (jobs.js:144). A file that just grows never wakes it. So either join writes one file per admission, which is what I'd pick, or the monitor re-reads when you open it.

A BUG, found by wsl-claude and verified by me. It touches a core gate, so it's your call. The shell refuses to serve the node's own relay-state/, which holds its private key (kernel.js:291). But it refuses only the top-level one. Every app server keeps its key at app-state/<app>/relay-state/identity.json (appServer.js:614), and ANY shell app, or the static route, can read that today. The fix is one line, refusing a 'relay-state' folder at any depth, plus a test. Go! = fix it now, on its own commit.

Yours. One fact: at HEAD, git grep -i github over spirit/run/app and js/appServer.js finds nothing, and no tracked file has 'join' in its name. So join isn't in the tree, and nothing logs GitHub ids today.
